argument_summary: The present record does not support a clean, caveat-free certification. It does support a narrower position: certification is defensible only on a qualified basis because aggregate launch readiness is met, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the record contains a defined mitigation direction consistent with measurement-and-monitoring guidance. The audit concern is strongest as to clean compliance, not as to any certification at all. The unresolved merchant dispute weakness should be treated as a disclosed limitation or explicit caveat rather than as a basis to characterize the entire certification position as unsupported.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is offered as a policy override. The narrower point is governance efficiency: if the remaining issue can be handled through an explicit caveat and disclosure treatment, escalation beyond that may be unnecessary because the admissible dispute is about the form of certification support, not about whether the release is wholly unevidenced.
claims_about_policy: The policy text sets a specific threshold for certification without material caveats: either no material weakness remains, or there is an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. That threshold is not met on the current admissible record because the runbook is still draft and missing required fields, and the merchant dispute slice remains below target. At the same time, the same policy text distinguishes disclosure obligations from overall risk-management support. Aggregate readiness evidence and monitoring direction do not eliminate the disclosure requirement, but they do support a caveated certification position if the unresolved slice issue is acknowledged as a material limitation rather than omitted.
concessions: The current record does not support clean certification without material caveats.
The merchant dispute support slice remains below target, concentrated in chargeback evidence summarization.
The mitigation runbook is draft and lacks the final owner and alert threshold required by policy for approved mitigation treatment.
The model-card draft cannot accurately say there are no known material limitations if this slice issue is material for a named launch use case.
